messages:
olivia: Heads-up — after last night's BMC rollout (v2.3.9) in eu-west rack-12, ~30 nodes show OOB NIC 'down' while host OS shows link up. GPU pool autoscaler isolated a bunch of nodes. logs:
```
[host=eu-west-r12-042] bmc: sfp negotiation timeout: PHY state stuck=0x4
ipmi: link state: DOWN, link training fail
[host=eu-west-r12-079] bmc: sfp rx error count spike 4291
```
Anyone else seeing SFP negotiation hang?

sam: I see the same in prometheus: `bmc_oob_link_errors` spikes around 00:15 UTC. Query — are these all Mellanox NICs or mixed? If Mellanox, could be firmware regression.

olivia: Mostly Mellanox SN2010 on those racks; a few Broadcoms mixed in. We rolled the BMC image to `v2.3.9-rc` last night, included the secureboot key staging change. Rollout window 00:00-02:00.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2024-4537 — "eu-west rack-12: BMC SFP negotiation hang" — paging eng-infra.

raj: Quick mitigation idea — try forcing re-negotiation via a soft BMC reset or toggling the PHY from the BMC: `ipmitool raw 0x32 0x48 0x01` (example sequence). Also bouncing the ToR port usually forces the PHY to retrain without a host reboot.

marie: Do we know if the secure-boot staging touched any NVRAM layout that could clobber PHY params? Release notes hinted at a KMS keystore migration that writes NVRAM.

kai: I'll take network side. I can do scheduled port-bounces on affected ToRs but prefer we try soft resets first to avoid broad switch churn. I'll collect `ethtool -m` SFP EEPROM dumps and SFP vendor ids.

sam: Scheduler impact: k8s marked 29 nodes NotReady, drained ~12 GPU pods. Autoscaler spun up 8 replacement nodes in us-west fallback at higher price. Early cost estimate: ~$3.2k/hr spike while we run replacements. Finance FYI?

marie: Can we do a canary rollback of the BMC image on a few nodes to confirm? If rollback clears it, we stop the rollout.

olivia: Soft-reset test on `eu-west-r12-042`: `bmc-reset --soft eu-west-r12-042` — link came back after ~27s and GPUs rejoined. But soft-reset on `eu-west-r12-079` didn't recover. Different SFP vendor behavior.

raj: Proposed plan:
1) Pause current rollout (olivia)
2) Canary-rollback BMC on 5 nodes (kai + olivia)
3) If rollback fixes >80% of canary, roll back next 2 batches and halt rollout
4) If rollback doesn't fix, coordinate ToR port bounce + per-host BMC soft-reset sequence
5) Add monitoring alert for BMC SFP negotiation timeout and SFP vendor mismatch
Who's owning network port bounces?

kai: I can own port bounces after we confirm list. Will script `switch-cli bounce port` per ToR and collect logs. Also grabbing SFP EEPROM dumps now.

olivia: Pausing deployment now. I'll push the affected-host list to #eng-network and attach the runbook note. Note: we did not toggle `secureboot` state — only staged keys. But I'll triple-check NVRAM migration logs.

oncall-bot: INC-2024-4537 updated: priority P1 -> P2 after partial recovery (5 nodes back).

sam: Scheduler team — marking replacement nodes for reclamation when clusters reach steady state. :thumbsup:

marie: After we resolve, let's add a BMC canary preflight: verify SFP negotiation health across vendors before rolling the image wide. Also add a flag to abort rollout on >10% oob_link_errors.

olivia: Thanks everyone — will follow up with postmortem once we confirm root cause (firmware vs NVRAM migration vs SFP vendor interaction).
